about: The golden fixture for account_store: the encrypted account store's crypto,
mls/core/src/account_store.rs (read its header for the why).
GENERATED by mls/core/tests/account_store_fixture.rs from fixed nonces and a
fixed ephemeral, with the Rust-only *_with seal variants. Do not edit by hand;
regenerate with PEACHY_WRITE_ACCOUNT_STORE_FIXTURE=1 (see that file's header).
Only OPENING is golden: a real seal takes a fresh nonce every time, so four
clients must agree on what a given value opens to and on every refusal.
Every expected plaintext / account key is the INPUT the generator sealed.
Replayed in Rust (mls/core/tests/account_store_fixture.rs), wasm
(mls/wasm/tests/node/account-store.test.mjs) and Swift
(AccountStoreFixtureTests.swift), and in Peachy's Android client in Kotlin,
each through the shared fixture door and the binding's own doors where it
has them (storeOpen, accountKeyAcceptHybrid).
KEY MATERIAL IS SYNTHESISED, NEVER REAL:
a1a1..a1  the account key;  a2a2..a2  another account's key
1111..11 (16)  a contact record's id;  2222..22 (16)  a chat record's id
0000..00 (16)  MANIFEST_ID
1111..11 (32)  Ada's phone, the APPROVING device's Ed25519 seed
3333..33  the new laptop, the RECIPIENT's seed
4444..44  a device that approved nothing;  5555..55  a bystander device
7777..77  a made-up static key (the forgery case)
5e5e..5e  the box's ephemeral X25519 secret;  6666..66  its nonce
5f5f..5f  a link secret, for the inner opener's version-2 cases (no client
sends one);  6060..60  a guessed one
0101.., 0202.. ... (12)  the record nonces;  7070.. to 7373..  the note nonces
9999..99 (16)  a self-note's id;  6a1c0e52-..  the phone's device id
boxAccept: the crate's inner opener (account_key_accept in
mls/core/src/account_store.rs), replayed through the fixture door only. A
version-2 box opens only with the link secret handed in, and no client seals
one; a version-1 box only from the approver whose number the person picked
on the device, or under the device's own switch for server-run approvals.
boxAcceptHybrid: the new device's door (account_key_accept_hybrid). A
version-3 box opens only from the approver whose number the person picked;
the device's own switch never opens one. A version-1 box opens only under the
device's own switch, from any listed approver, and never otherwise, even from
a confirmed approver. A version-2 box never opens there.
noteSender / noteOpenSigned: the signed note (format 0x02, domain
"peachy self note v2"), sealed and signed by the sending device. noteSender
says which device the note claims sent it; noteOpenSigned believes it only
under that device's key (deviceId, senderKeyHex), issued at most seven days
before nowMs and at most ten minutes after it.
transferKeyOpen: the key of a history hand-off's document, sealed to the
device it is handed to (domain "peachy transfer key v1"). It opens only with
that device's seed and its own device id; the account key is no help, and an
account-key box never opens as a transfer box nor the reverse. 7c7c..7c is
the attachment key.
expectError is a substring of the refusal's message.

cases.why: k(id) = HKDF-SHA256(account_key, salt empty, info "peachy store v1" 0x00 id).
The manifest's key: the same derivation over the reserved all-zero id.
Same id, another account: a different key.
An id is exactly 16 bytes; anything else is a caller's bug, not an id.
cases.expectError: a store id must be exactly 16 bytes, got 15

cases.why: An account key is exactly 32 bytes.
cases.expectError: an account_key must be exactly 32 bytes, got 31

cases.why: An empty plaintext pads to one whole block: 0x80 then 255 zeros.
255 bytes plus the 0x80 marker fill exactly one 256-byte block.
256 bytes leave no room for the marker, so the padding spills into a second block.
1000 bytes pad to 1024: four blocks. Plaintext bytes include 0x00 and 0x80, which unpad must leave alone.
A record in the shape the clients write: UTF-8 JSON.
The manifest is sealed exactly like a record, under MANIFEST_ID (16 zero bytes).
The server serves the contact's value under the chat's id. The id is in the key AND the AAD.
cases.expectError: does not open under this key and id

cases.why: The manifest served as a record: refused, like any other wrong id.
cases.expectError: does not open under this key and id

cases.why: Another account's key.
cases.expectError: does not open under this key and id

cases.why: One bit of the tag flipped.
cases.expectError: does not open under this key and id

cases.expectError: does not open under this key and id

cases.why: One bit of the nonce flipped.
cases.expectError: does not open under this key and id

cases.why: 0x01 is the only format; a value from a future format is refused by name, not misread.
cases.expectError: unknown store format version 0x02

cases.why: A 15-byte id is refused before anything is decrypted.
cases.expectError: a store id must be exactly 16 bytes, got 15

cases.why: Shorter than version + nonce + tag + one padding block (285 bytes).
cases.expectError: a sealed store value is too short: 284 bytes, at least 285

cases.why: Ada's phone (seed 1111..) boxes the account key for her new laptop (seed 3333..).
THE case. The server claims a different approver; the static-static half of the agreement does not match, so it does not open.
cases.expectError: does not open for this device, approver and device id

cases.expectError: does not open for this device, approver and device id

cases.expectError: does not open for this device, approver and device id

cases.expectError: does not open for this device, approver and device id

cases.why: 0x01 and 0x02 are the only box formats.
cases.expectError: unknown account key box format version 0x03

cases.why: A box is exactly 93 bytes.
cases.expectError: an account key box must be exactly 93 bytes, got 92

cases.why: A device id is never empty.
cases.expectError: a device_id must not be empty

cases.why: Ada's phone scanned the laptop's QR code and sealed with the link secret it carried (5f5f..): a version-2 box, which the laptop opens with the secret it showed.
The plain opener reads version 1 only: a box keyed with a link secret goes through boxAccept.
cases.expectError: format version 0x02; this call reads 0x01

cases.why: THE case for the QR path. A server runs a device of its own (7777..), lists it as an approver, and seals its own account key with a secret it made up. The laptop opens with the secret it showed, and it does not open.
cases.expectError: does not open for this device, approver and device id

cases.why: A version-2 box on a device that showed no QR code has nothing to open it with.
cases.expectError: this device showed no QR code

cases.why: A link secret is exactly 32 bytes.
cases.expectError: a link_secret must be exactly 32 bytes, got 31

cases.why: THE case for the number path. The server's own device (7777..) seals a plain box that opens under its own key; the laptop showed a QR code nobody scanned and confirmed no approver, so it refuses.
cases.expectError: an approver the person did not confirm on this device

cases.why: The person picked Ada's phone's number on the laptop: a plain box from that key, and only that key, is accepted.
The person confirmed Ada's phone; the box is from another listed device. Confirming one approver vouches for no other.
cases.expectError: an approver the person did not confirm on this device

cases.why: The device's own switch (a test server it was built for, or a sign-in with a fictional number): a plain box from any listed approver is accepted.
The switch skips the person's confirmation, not the cryptography: a box claimed for another approver still does not open.
cases.expectError: does not open for this device, approver and device id

cases.why: The laptop posted an X-Wing link key (seed 5a5a..) with its nonce, signed by its own key; Ada's phone, whose number the person picked, sealed a version-3 box to it. The box key mixes both X25519 agreements with the X-Wing secret, so recording the pairing today and breaking X25519 later opens nothing.
The device's own switch opens a version-1 box from any listed approver, never a version-3 box: that opens only from the approver whose number the person picked here.
cases.expectError: an approver the person did not confirm on this device

cases.why: A sound box, but the person confirmed no approver on this device: refused before any cryptography.
cases.expectError: an approver the person did not confirm on this device

cases.why: A version-3 box on a device that posted no link key has nothing to open it with.
cases.expectError: a box sealed to a link key, and this device posted none

cases.why: THE case for the link key. A server that swapped in a link key of its own (seed 5b5b..) cannot make the approver's box open on the laptop: the laptop opens with the seed it drew, and the box does not open.
cases.expectError: does not open for this device, approver, link key and device id

cases.why: One bit of the X-Wing encapsulation flipped: the KEM secret differs, and the encapsulation is also the AES-GCM associated data, so it does not open.
cases.expectError: does not open for this device, approver, link key and device id

cases.why: A version-3 box is exactly 1213 bytes.
cases.expectError: a version-3 account key box must be exactly 1213 bytes, got 1212

cases.why: THE downgrade. A version-1 box from the confirmed approver is refused, so a server that strips the link key from the pairing gets no X25519-only box accepted by this door.
cases.expectError: an X25519-only account key box, and this build takes only the post-quantum box

cases.why: The approvals a test server makes itself seal version 1; the device's own switch still lets one open.
Ada's phone seals the key of the history it hands her new laptop (seed 3333..) to the laptop's signing key and row.

cases.why: The phone's read note, opened against the phone's own key, at the moment it was sent.
The oldest a note may be: exactly seven days after it was issued.
A millisecond past seven days: a note the server kept back and delivers again is refused.
cases.expectError: stale

cases.expectError: dated ahead
